criteria.true: The <property> of <part> looks the same: a person comparing the images side by side would see no difference in it.
criteria.false: The <property> of <part> is visibly different between the images, or <part> is missing from one of them.

check.0.instructions: In `screenshot`, does <part> meet this requirement: <property>? The specification it belongs to is in `specification`.

`frames` are 1 frames of a screen recording, in order of time (`seconds` is the time of each). Looking at how the picture changes from one frame to the next, does <part> meet this requirement: <property>? The specification it belongs to is in `specification`.

criteria.true: From frame to frame, <part> does what the requirement says.
criteria.false: From frame to frame, <part> does something other than what the requirement says, or the frames do not show it.

complexity.level.instructions: The images in `reference_images` are references for something that is going to be built to match them (an interface, a 3D model, a scene, an animation). How complex is it to build it so that it matches them? Rate the work of reproducing what the images show, not how important or well known the subject is.
criteria: A single plain shape or flat graphic with almost nothing to it and no fine detail, such as a plain cube, a solid-colour logo or one basic button.
A few plain elements laid out simply, with little detail: a basic screen with a handful of standard controls, or an object made of a few primitive shapes.
A moderate number of distinct parts with some detail or styling: an ordinary app screen, a recognisable object of several components, or a small scene with a few materials.
Many distinct parts with fine detail, layered materials, lighting or effects: a dense interface, a detailed model, or a scene with several kinds of surfaces.

A very large amount of intricate detail: a whole city or environment, an organic or highly detailed model with many parts, a scene with many interacting effects, or a screen of many interacting elements.

scoring: An item with checks: each check holds (the part is the same as in the reference, or the frames meet the requirement) or does not. A check that holds is right when it is judged PASS, a check that does not hold when it is judged FAIL; UNSURE is neither right nor wrong. The item is `correct` when none of its checks is judged the wrong way round (`false-pass`: a part that differs judged PASS, which must not happen; `false-fail`: a part that is the same judged FAIL), `exact` when every check is right: an item all UNSURE is correct and not exact, so read `exact` and the figures, not `correct` alone. A complexity item: right when the level the group reads as is in gold.accept, exact when it is gold.level; whether the groups read in the order of their rank is in the figures (`complexity`). The verdicts are the mod's (PASS from 0.8, FAIL up to 0.2 for a screenshot and up to 0.4 for the frames of a motion, as of 2026-10-15; against a reference a PASS is the crop's and a whole image only fails, ADR 0008); the raw probabilities are kept with each answer, and `thresholds` gives what other bars would have said. Controls are the items in which nothing differs.

about.variants: `mod`: as the mod asks with the run's decision model: against a reference, Jev gets the checks and the Box questions in the first request and the zoomed re-check on the crops after it, pplx the first request alone; a motion is its frames in one request against its spec; a group of references is the complexity reading. `whole`: the first request alone with every decision model, so that what the zoomed re-check adds can be read from the two. `criteria`: the first request alone, each check with criteria for both sides and its images named in the question (Nace's guide), the mod's wording beside it as `plain.<i>` (its probability is each check's `plain`); a motion is 8 frames.
about.images: The experiment's pictures (2026-10-15), copied into eval/datasets/visual-check/; sized and cut as the mod does (core/image-files.ts, core/zoom-review.ts, sips). A motion is its 12 frames as files (8 of them for pplx), not a recording: the mod's ffmpeg is not run.
